question: At which place did the Congress declare the resolution of Purna Swaraj in its session in 1929?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lahore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Congress session of 1929 was held at Lahore from 29th to 31st December.
 
• It was during this session that the Indian National Congress, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the historic resolution of Purna Swaraj or complete independence from British rule.
 
• The resolution was officially adopted on December 31, 1929.
 
• The declaration of Purna Swaraj led to the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purna Swaraj**

 
 
• Purna Swaraj, or complete independence, was declared by the Indian National Congress as the goal for India’s freedom struggle against British colonial rule.
 
• It was a significant shift from the earlier demand for dominion status within the British Empire.
 
• January 26, 1930, was declared as "Independence Day" and was to be celebrated by the people of India as the day of complete independence.
 
• This declaration set the stage for more intense and widespread movements, including the famous Salt March led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• Founded in 1885, the Indian National Congress (INC) played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The INC was instrumental in organizing and leading efforts against British rule through various movements and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• Key leaders of the INC included Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, among others.
 
• The INC was the principal leader in the struggle for independence, which was finally achieved in 1947.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement**
 
 
• Launched in 1930, the Civil Disobedience Movement was a major campaign of nonviolent resistance against British rule.
 
• It began with the Salt March, where Gandhi and his followers marched to the Arabian Sea coast to produce salt from seawater, defying British laws.
 
• The movement saw widespread participation from various sections of Indian society, including women and rural populations.
 
• It marked a significant escalation in the Indian struggle for independence, leading to numerous arrests and acts of defiance against colonial laws.
